minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved added flow for two basement bedrooms and discussed rising FY28 costs and user fees.
minutes.summary: The commission approved extra sewer flow for a basement bedroom addition at a single-family home. Staff reviewed the FY27 year-to-date budget, early FY28 planning, pump station aging, and a new discharge permit's cost. The demand fee rate decision and prior minutes were put off until the full board is present, and the public hearing date was left unsettled.

public_comment.topic: A former sewer commissioner was listening only; the chair appealed for a new commission member.

votes.motion: Approve additional sewer flow for two added bedrooms at the Prep/P Street address

budget_items.topic: Additional sewer flow charge for two bedrooms
budget_items.what_was_said: The fee for the added bedrooms was said to match the normal fee structure.
The budget is not in awful shape, but capital funds are the last major line left. Retained earnings may be needed to pay the pump station contract.
New permit requirements were not in the budget and the engineering estimate was a shock. A way was found to pay this year.
Capital planning, engineering, electricity, outsourcing, stabilization transfer and connection fee lines are expected to rise.
Betterment revenue is falling as people pay ahead or sell, so user fees must rise to stay stable.
User fees are now most of revenue, and fees for FY28 and FY29 need to rise.
The cost estimate for the Lemonster Road station work was cited.

decisions.decision: Prior minutes will be approved at the next meeting because a member was absent from the earlier meeting.
The sewer demand fee rate decision will wait until the full commission is present.
The December 8th meeting will be used for the budget discussion in person; the public hearing on rates is expected in January.
Schedule: Dec 8 hybrid at 6 pm, Jan 12 Zoom, Feb 9 Zoom.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission approved additional sewer flow for two added basement bedrooms at a single-family home.
Staff said new discharge permit engineering costs were not budgeted for FY27, and a way was found to pay them this year.
Staff said FY28 lines for capital planning, engineering, electricity and other items are expected to rise, and user fees for FY28 and FY29 need to rise.
Betterment revenue is falling as people pay ahead or sell, leaving user fees as most of revenue.
The sewer demand fee rate decision was put off until the full commission is present; the rate hearing is expected in January.

why_it_matters: Sewer users should expect higher fees in FY28 and FY29, because a falling betterment revenue stream and rising permit, engineering and electricity costs leave user fees to carry more of the system.
The demand fee rate and a public rate hearing are still ahead, so residents on the sewer system will have a chance to weigh in before rates are set.
